content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching provision exists anywhere in the Agreement; § 12.3 affirmatively confirms it.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" return no covenant restricting either Party from soliciting or hiring the other's personnel. § 12.3 expressly confirms that Customer has made no no-hire commitment and preserves Customer's freedom to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. The Agreement therefore sits at our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), and no redline is warranted. Note that § 12.4 imposes a 24-month non-compete on Customer, but that is a competitive-restriction/exclusivity term addressed under the applicable rule, not a non-solicitation of employees, so we do not flag it here.
